children: An official gauge of China's manufacturing activity rebounded by more than expected in August as output and market demand recovered, suggesting that the slowdown in manufacturing may hit bottom in July.
China's official manufacturing purchasing managers index in August rose to 49.8 from 49.2 in July, said the National Bureau of Statistics on Monday.

The result was the second consecutive month the PMI has been below the 50 threshold, even though it beat the 49.5 tipped by a Wall Street Journal survey of economists. A reading below 50 signals a contraction in activity, while a reading above 50 indicates an expansion.

The rise to the cusp of the 50 mark could help reassure Chinese policymakers, who pledged additional measures to support the economy after second-quarter economic growth slowed to below Beijing's target.
Regulators also introduced rules last week to lower credit barriers for homebuyers and property developers alike, to help address a key drag on domestic demand.

"We expect a further improvement in economic momentum over the rest of the year, as adverse weather fades and local governments accelerate their already-budgeted spending," said Nguyen Hoang Nam, an economist at Capital Economics.
Both the factory production and new orders subindexes moved above the 50 mark in August, lifting the headline index.

The production subindex rose to 50.4, compared with 49.9 in July. The subindex for total new orders increased to 50.6, up from 48.5 in July, while new export orders also rebounded to 50.1 from 49.6 in July.

By sector, high-tech and equipment manufacturing--including electrical machinery and equipment--saw output and new orders subindexes climb above 53.0, reflecting rapid improvements in supply and demand.

On the other hand, heavy and raw-material industries, such as chemical raw materials and ferrous metal smelting and processing, saw both sub-indices drop below the 50-mark threshold, signaling muted market activity.
China's nonmanufacturing PMI, which covers both service and construction activity, stayed unchanged at 49.0 in August, the statistics bureau said.
The subindex tracking service activity remained unchanged at 49.3 in August, while the construction subindex slipped to 46.9 from 47.0.

Heavy rainfalls and extreme weather dragged on construction activity last month, said the statistics bureau. It added that weakness in wholesale, retail and financial services continued to weigh on the service PMI last month, said the statistics bureau.
